paper.title: Achieving Counterfactual Fairness for Causal Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual causal bandit with soft intervention and d-separation set (D-UCB setting)
unmapped: Known causal graph (Markovian SCM) with a d-separation set W separating reward from arm/user features
Conditional distributions P(z | x_{t,a}) are known to the learner
Learner observes the realized value of the d-separation set W each round
Policies are soft interventions on arm features; finite policy space; discrete variables
settings.definition_quote: For each customer arrived at time $t\in [T]$ with feature vector $\mathbf{x}_t\in \mathcal{X}$, the algorithm recommends an item with features $\sa$ based on vector $\mathbf{x}_{t,a}$ ... observes the reward $r_t$ ... Similarly to \cite{lu2020regret}, we assume that distribution $P(\mathbf{z}| \x_{t,a})$ is known

settings.name_in_paper: Fair causal bandit with counterfactual fairness constraint (F-UCB setting)
unmapped: Known causal graph and known P(z | x_{t,a})
Each round's policy must satisfy a tau-counterfactual fairness constraint (conservative UCB of counterfactual discrepancy <= tau)
Existence of a safe policy pi_0 with Delta_{pi_0} <= tau every round (Assumption 3); learner uses tau and Delta_{pi_0}
Mean reward and fairness discrepancy in [0,1], 1-sub-Gaussian errors

symbols.W_dom: domain size |W| of the d-separation set W

conditions: holds w.p. at least 1-2 delta T |W| - exp(-|W| log^3(T)/(32 log(1/delta)))

source.label: thm:rb
source.quote: Given a causal graph $\mathcal{G}$, with probability at least $1-2\delta T |\mathbf{W}| - \exp(- \frac{|\mathbf{W}| \log^3(T)}{32\log(1/\delta)})$, the regret of D-UCB is bounded by \[   \mathcal{R}_T \leq \sqrt{|\mathbf{W}| T\log(T)}log(T) + \sqrt{32|\mathbf{W}|T \log(1/\delta)}   \] where $|\mathbf{W}|$ is the domain space of set $\W$.

results.notes: Regret defined as sum of mu_{a*} - mu_{a_t} with per-round optimal policy given context. Probability is unusual (depends on T).

symbols.W_dom: domain size |W| of the d-separation set W

conditions: holds w.p. at least 1-2|W|/T - exp(-|W| log^2(T)/64)

source.quote: By setting $\delta = 1/T^2$, the causal bandit algorithm achieves $\Tilde{O}(\sqrt{|\mathbf{W}| \cdot T})$ regret bound.

results.notes: Explicit constant 16 from the proof of the corollary; statement itself says O~(sqrt(|W| T)).

symbols.W_dom: domain size |W| of the d-separation set W

conditions: existence of safe policy pi_0 with Delta_{pi_0} <= tau each round
1-sub-Gaussian noise, means of reward and discrepancy in [0,1]
holds with probability at least 1 - delta_E

source.quote: Given a causal graph $\mathcal{G}$, let $\delta_E = 4|\mathbf{W}|T\delta$ and $\Delta_{\pi_0}$  denote the maximum fairness discrepancy of a safe policy $\pi_0$ across all rounds. Setting $\alpha_c = 1$ and $\alpha_r = \frac{2}{\tau - \Delta_{\pi_0}}$, with probability at least $1-\delta_E$, the cumulative regret of F-UCB is bounded by: ...
